description: Recommends new Residential Parking Program policy.
Policy would allow multi-unit residents permits.
Policy would introduce tiered permit pricing.

chips.text: Recommended
Permit pricing aims for administrative cost recovery.
Mayor Block questioned if recommendations truly modernize the program.
Residents in Caswell Hill, City Park, Varsity View affected by pilot.
Mayor Block felt recommendations lacked sufficient modernization.
New policy shifts RPP administration from bylaw to staff.
Unclear how much of City Park RPP zone is paid parking.
Varsity View Community Association proposed paid non-resident parking, revenue reinvestment.
Mayor Block opposed, citing lack of modernization and multi-unit permit concerns.
Policy change addresses equity concerns for multi-unit residents.
Mail-out ticketing pilot report due end of 2028.

speakers.name: CLinton Ekdahl
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Registered Parking Program and Proposed Alternative Solutions
said: Proposes paid parking for non-permitted vehicles in high-demand RPP areas.
Advocates for parking revenue reinvestment to achieve cost-revenue neutrality.
Suggests prohibiting motorists from resetting time limits by moving spaces.

speakers.name: Derek Cameron
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Residential Parking Permits
said: Current RPP proposal does little to curb non-resident parking demand.
Suggests charging non-residents an hourly fee to achieve 80% occupancy.
Recommends dedicating a portion of revenue to neighborhood improvements.

description: Explore fare adjustments, including monthly passes, graduate U-Pass, fare capping.
Continue implementing Open Payments for transit by late 2027.
Introduce regular four-year transit fare and UPass reviews.

chips.text: Recommended
Monthly pass rising to $100 on January 1st, up $17.
Councillor Ford questioned waiting two years for fare capping analysis.
Council moved to consider fare capping pilot sooner than staff recommended.
New policy sets four-year cycle for transit fare and UPass reviews.
Timing for next comprehensive transit fare review remains unplanned.
Bus Riders of Saskatoon criticized slow pace of fare capping and comprehensive review.
Mayor Block supported fare capping in spirit but preferred waiting for BRT data.
Graduate students pay more per month for U-Pass than undergraduates.
Administration committed to incorporating lessons learned into next fare review.

speakers.name: Sherry Tarasoff
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Considerations for Adjusting Transit Fares - November 2026 Update
said: Expedite open payments for easier, modern fare payment.
Implement fair capping sooner; waiting four years is a disservice.
Questioned return on investment of ridership growth initiatives.

speakers.name: Sunny Bui
speakers.organization: University of Saskatchewan Graduate Students Association
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Considerations for Adjusting Transit Fares - November 2026 Update
said: Deferring year-round U-Pass for grad students does not address current need.
Graduate students pay more per month for U-Pass than undergraduates.
Council should meet to provide options for spring/summer U-Pass access.

speakers.name: Robert Clipperton
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Considerations for Adjusting Transit Fares
said: Pleased with planned open payments for easier fare payment.
Supports regular, consistent fair reviews as standard practice.
2025 fair review was ineffective and lacked comprehensive engagement.

description: Committee recommends expropriating land for six BRT stations.
Negotiations with property owners for these sites stalled.
Decision deferred 30 days for further negotiation attempts.

chips.text: Recommended
Land acquisition costs for BRT stations are 100% city funded.
Councillor Pierce expressed concern about expropriation as "nuclear response".
Six property owners on 22nd Street and 8th Street are affected.
Public concerns about social disorder at heated shelters were not addressed.
Public speakers questioned necessity of expropriation and urged further negotiation.
Expropriation is ultimate exercise of governmental authority, requiring strict justification.
Administration promised one final negotiation attempt before expropriation.

speakers.name: Karen Kobussen
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: BRT Link Platform Station Property Acquisition Update
said: Heated shelters attract social disorder, loitering, littering.
Expropriation is not a last resort; other options exist.
Return to negotiating table for positive agreement with owners.

speakers.name: Henry Chan
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: BRT Link Platform Station Property Acquisition Update
said: Property and investment security for businesses is paramount.
Questioned if expropriation is necessity or bureaucratic impatience.
Extraordinary power of expropriation needs sufficient justification.

description: Accessibility Committee's 2027 plan and budget forwarded to Council.

chips.text: Recommended
Councillor McDonald questioned committee's mandate to act as resource to administration.
Councillor McDonald asked if administration can directly call on the committee.
Committee's work plan focuses on improving accessibility for residents with disabilities.
